construction engineering western michigan university kalamazoo mi 49008-5316 usa (269) 276-3210 what we do the michigan department of transportation established the research center of excellence on structural durability at western michigan university to partner with mdot in performing applied research, providing education and performing outreach. the partnership allows mdot to remain engaged in helping to shape the future of transportation in michigan, nationally and internationally. the continued cooperative efforts between mdot and wmu also help ensure that the transportation leaders of the future will be prepared to meet the many challenges that lie ahead. the center evaluates the materials, design, construction, repair and maintenance of highway structures in harsh climates to improve their durability and prolong service life. the studies conducted by the center integrate field studies, laboratory testing and analytical simulation to understand complex phenomena that result in aging and deterioration of transportation infrastructure. the center collaborates with research centers and individual researchers nationally and internationally. the center also collaborates with private consultants and companies to enhance quality of research results, and research results delivery and implementation process. research, courses and publications research concrete durability ph.d., p.e.; yufeng hu, ph.d., p.e. duration: october 2022 – september 2024 bridge inspection engineers and consultants submit requests for action (rfas) due to safety concerns associated with steel girder and prestressed concrete (psc) beam end conditions. region bridge engineers review rfas and bring forward to the bridge rfa coordination committee (brfacc) for deliberations. this project focuses on developing guidelines and tools for bridge inspection engineers, region bridge engineers, and the other members of the brfacc to help them streamline the rfa submission and evaluation process. this will help overcome programming and resource allocation challenges while ensuring public safety and avoiding potentially unnecessary restrictions on the motoring public. these tools and guidelines will help the load rating unit (lru) load rate deteriorated and repaired beam ends. operational baseline and structural health monitoring for the 2nd avenue network arch bridge funding agency: the michigan department of transportation pi: upul attanayake, ph.d., p.e. duration: january 2022 –may 2024 a skewed, unbraced network tied-arch bridge was constructed to carry the 2 nd avenue over i-94. this 265 ft long, 96.5 ft wide structure carries vehicular traffic, bicycles, and pedestrians in separate dedicated lanes. the unique structural configuration and the use of innovative accelerated bridge construction (abc) technique made this one of the most significant projects in bridge engineering. the bridge skeleton, consisting of trapezoidal steel arch ribs, tie girders, end diaphragms, and steel floor beams was assembled in a staging area near the bridge site. in implementing abc, the bridge skeleton was moved into alignment using self-propelled modular transporters (spmts) during a 7-day closure of i-94. following the spmt move, including lifting and sliding activities, and the placement of the skeleton on permanent bearings, the remaining construction activities were completed. the ultimate goals of this project are to establish (i) the final state of stress at the end of the 2 nd avenue over i-94 bridge construction, (ii) the operational baseline by conducting a static live load test, (iii) stress envelopes for the safe operation of the structure, and (iv) a functional monitoring system and necessary tools for data-driven maintenance upul attanayake, ph.d., p.e. duration: 01/2002- 12/ 2002 publications: final report courses and workshops for official, current semester course information, consult the wmu catalog . undergraduate courses cce 3080—civil engineering materials this course is 3.0 credit hours with 2.0 lecture hours and 3.0 lab hours weekly. the course focuses on the study of constituents of materials used in civil and construction engineering, physical and mechanical properties of materials, and laboratory and field methods for the evaluation of materials. aci field technician grade i certification: we have established a process in collaboration with the michigan concrete association (mca) for wmu cce students to obtain the american concrete institute (aci) concrete field testing technician - grade i certification at the end of the course. cce 3360—soil mechanics this course is 3.0 credit hours with 2.0 lecture hours and 3.0 lab hours weekly. the course focuses on the study of the physical properties of soil and the behavior of soil masses subjected to various types of forces. further, this course will focus on origin of soil and its grain size distribution, ability to drain water, compressibility, shear strength, and load-bearing capacity. during this course, students will learn application of laws of mechanics and hydraulics to engineering problems dealing with different soil types. this course is 3.0 credit hours with 2.0 lecture hours and 3.0 lab hours weekly. cce 4561—foundation and earth retaining structure design this course covers the analysis, design, and construction aspects of shallow and deep foundations and retaining structures. the main objective is to enable students to select, analyze, and design an appropriate foundation and/or an earth retaining structure for a given scenario. this course is 3.0 credit hours. graduate courses cce 5460—design of timber structures structural behavior of wood under loads; application of current timber design codes; design of structural components and systems in wood; mechanical properties of wood fasteners and connections. this course is 3.0 credit hours. cce 5460—design of timber structures structural behavior of wood under loads; application of current timber design codes; design of structural components and systems in wood; mechanical properties of wood fasteners and connections. this course is 3.0 credit hours. cce 6470—bridge engineering the course focuses on analysis, design, and rating of bridges as per the aashto specifications/guidelines. simplified analysis procedures as well as use of software tools will be covered. this course is 3.0 credit hours. cce 6480—finite element applications the course focuses on the study of finite element applications to common engineering problems including linear static, heat transfer, flow through porous medium, seepage, resistivity, etc. during the course, abaqus is used as the analysis tool. this course is 3.0 credit hours. cce 6510—structural systems and assessment the course focuses on (1) behavior of structural systems made of concrete, steel, and precast components or a combination thereof and (2) structural condition assessment by visual inspection, nondestructive evaluation (nde) techniques, and destructive testing techniques or a combination thereof. students will be given an opportunity to conduct investigations using some nde techniques. this course is 3.0 credit hours. publications journal publications mazumder, a. f., attanayake, u., and berke, n. s. directory contact us civil and construction engineering western michigan university kalamazoo mi 49008-5316 usa (269) 276-3210 why study civil and construction engineering? civil and construction engineering is the broadest of the engineering professions and is the stem from which most other branches of engineering have developed. civil and construction engineering involves the planning, design, construction, maintenance and operation of facilities and systems to control and improve the environment for modern civilizations. this includes projects of major importance such as bridges, transportation systems, buildings, ports and water distribution systems. i have always enjoyed subjects related to the stem field and have had a deep passion for helping the environment. civil engineering combines both of these. —lila rode, civil engineering our vision mission we provide the opportunity for civil and construction engineering students to obtain state-of-the-art engineering knowledge and skills through student-centered education and research. teamwork, professionalism and life-long learning are hallmarks of our educational programs. faculty research is to provide innovative solutions to civil and construction engineering problems of regional, national and global significance. vision be a leader in civil and construction engineering education integrating design throughout the curriculum. upon graduation, students will be able to perform and contribute to the global civil and construction engineering community. be a recognized center for life-long learning in civil and construction engineering and for providing innovative research and expertise that improves our way of life. goals goals a high quality faculty : hire and retain a highly qualified, diverse and motivated faculty who support and enhance our aspirations for excellence. excellence in engineering education : maintain an innovative and flexible curriculum founded in the fundamentals that emphasizes design and teamwork, and is responsive to the needs of our stakeholders. excellence in research and scholarship : develop and maintain a nationally and internationally recognized research program in at least three areas of civil engineering solving problems relevant to the national infrastructure and serving the state of michigan. contribute to life-long learning opportunities : to meet the ever-changing technological and scientific needs of practicing engineers, we will provide opportunities for engineers in the region to continue their professional development and will serve as a resource for technology transfer regarding relevant issues related to professional practice. building your career our graduates are ready to take on challenges and advance engineering and applied sciences fields like civil and construction engineering. they are found in important roles in an array of companies worldwide. our alumni when you attend western michigan university to pursue a degree in civil and construction engineering , you will join a growing group of alumni who are impacting our field. alumni such as paul albanelli, b.s.’81, the senior advisor for albanelli cement contractors, inc. albanelli joined the family-owned concrete contracting company full-time after graduating from the construction supervision and management program at wmu. after 50 years of building with concrete, albanelli sold his shares of the company to his son, alberto, who begins the fourth generation to lead albanelli cement. albanelli received a college of engineering and applied sciences alumni excellence award in 2024. read more about albanelli and other award recipients looking to get involved? contact julie loncharte. apply to wmu schedule your campus visit request info footer menu
